Class FormFieldElement

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<FormFieldElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.FormFieldElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class FormFieldElement extends StyledElement<FormFieldElement>
A form field element that pairs a label with an input control.

FormFieldElement reduces boilerplate by combining a label and input into a single element with consistent layout and styling. It supports multiple field types including text inputs, checkboxes, toggles, and select dropdowns.

Basic Usage

// With TextInputState
formField("Full name", nameState)
    .labelWidth(14)
    .rounded()
    .borderColor(Color.DARK_GRAY)
    .focusedBorderColor(Color.CYAN)

// With FormState
formField("Email", FORM.textField("email"))
    .placeholder("you@example.com")
    .validate(Validators.required(), Validators.email())

CSS Child Selectors

  • FormFieldElement-label - The label text style (default: dim)
  • FormFieldElement-input - The input wrapper (delegates to child element's CSS)
  • FormFieldElement-error - The inline error message style (default: red)

      public FormFieldElement arrowNavigation(boolean enabled)
      Enables arrow key navigation for this field.

      When enabled, pressing Up/Down arrows in text fields and boolean fields will return EventResult.FOCUS_PREVIOUS/EventResult.FOCUS_NEXT to navigate between fields. Select fields still use Up/Down for selection.

      Parameters:
      enabled - true to enable arrow navigation
      Returns:
      this element for chaining

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size
